bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: U.S. tariffs on stainless steel; Saudi duty risk post-local production (10%); domestic water pipeline tender delays; nuclear spool execution volatility; European quota/tariff changes from Jan 2026
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and execution-focused; highlights order visibility, capacity utilization, and global expansion; avoids margin breakdowns but confirms growth trajectory; acknowledges domestic demand softness but emphasizes export and capex-led growth
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: RFSS's INR 500cr order book is entirely nuclear and will be fully executed by Q1FY27 — next order inflection likely in Q3FY26; Saudi plant will export mother hollows from India, preserving higher Indian margins; RTL's U.S. exports are minimal despite Timken supply
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Company remains debt free on standalone basis"; strengths slide cites a strong balance sheet, healthy cash flows, a robust credit profile and consistent returns to shareholders.
- Dividend per share across FY22-FY26 is shown as Rs 9, Rs 9.33 (after bonus issue of 1:2), Rs 14, Rs 14 and Rs 10, with dividend % of 467%, 600%, 700%, 700% and 500%.
- A 1:2 bonus issue is footnoted in the FY23 dividend column.
- Reinvestment is running heavy: three greenfield/brownfield plants were completed or are due within 12 months across the parent and subsidiaries, plus a KSA greenfield to March 2028.
- Group builds reach through stakes rather than wholly-owned scale: RFSS 51% (India, 2023), Ravi Technoforge 75% (India; 2022 initial, 2025 stake increased to 75%), Ratnamani Middle East Company LLC 75% (KSA, 2025), with 100%-owned marketing/stock-and-sale arms Ratnamani Inc. (USA, 2014), Ratnamani Middle East Pipes Trading LLC OPC (UAE, 2024) and Ratnamani Trade EU AG (Switzerland with a warehouse in Germany, 2024).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as the "Largest Player of the Stainless Steel Tubes & Pipes (high end applications) in India" and "One of the Leading Player for Carbon Steel Welded Pipes in India", with 40+ years of experience and 3,300+ employees.
- Serves 20+ industries in 28+ countries, spanning oil & gas, refinery & petrochemical, cross-country gas and water pipelines, atomic/nuclear and thermal power, LNG, desalination, aerospace, defence, semiconductors and data centres.
- Quality positioned as a moat: NABL ISO/IEC 17025, ILAC-accredited laboratories and global certifications, plus approvals from end clients, EPC contractors and process licensors.
- Claims to be the "First in India to supply hydrogen-compliant pipes", building capabilities for new energy and offshore applications.
- CRISIL rating of AA/Positive; certified as a Great Place to Work in India based on the Trust Index survey.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demand environment] CEO cites lower government spending on infrastructure projects including the water segment, plus the ongoing geopolitical situation in the Middle East impacting demand, project execution and raw material supplies; exports "witnessed encouraging growth" and enquiry levels across key markets continue to improve.
- [Subsidiary credit] RTL's credit rating for long-term bank facilities was upgraded from CARE A to CARE A+; RFSS bank borrowings are credit rated CRISIL AA-.
- [JV partner] RFSS is a joint venture with Technoenergy AG, Switzerland, holding entity of FINOW GmbH, Germany, which has specialised in nuclear spools for over a century.
- [Promoter-led board] The board is heavily family-anchored — Prakash M. Sanghvi (Chairman & MD), Jayanti M. Sanghvi (Joint MD), Shantilal M. Sanghvi (WTD), Manoj P. Sanghvi (WTD & CEO) and Prashant J. Sanghvi (WTD) — alongside five independent directors.
- [Market capitalisation] Market capitalisation of Rs 17500 Crores as of June 30, 2026 (deck's own stated figure).

deepdive.thesis: Strong order inflow in carbon steel (INR 750cr Q2) and nuclear spools (INR 500cr book) is driving momentum, while Saudi cold-finishing plant and RFSS capacity expansion are key value creators; consolidated revenue guidance of INR 7,500cr in 2-3 years hinges on execution of these capex projects.

open.item: Executing a ₹1,380 Crores capex programme to expand Carbon Steel Circumferentially welded Submerged Arc Welded (CSAW) Pipes capacity from 48,000 MT to 75,000 MT and establish a new 1,00,000 MT Helical Submerged Arc Welded (HSAW)/spiral pipe facility, targeting mechanical readiness by Q1 FY2026-27, positioning the Company for Middle East mega-projects and domestic cross-country pipeline bids.
Expansion for high-thickness Circumferential Submerged Arc Welded (C-SAW) and Helical Submerged Arc Welded (H-SAW) pipes at Kutch is targeted for completion by June 2026.
Phase II of the Odisha plant, a coating plant designed to support the HSAW production line, is due for completion by July 2026, enabling integrated downstream processing at the site.
Board recommended a dividend of ₹10.00 per equity share for FY2025-26 (previous year ₹14.00), totalling a payout of ₹70.09 Crores, subject to shareholder approval at the 42nd AGM on August 18, 2026.
Ravi Technoforge's new high-speed hot-forming facility, expanding into the large-volume bearing rings segment with new automotive component capabilities, has a commissioning target of March 2027.
Transformative ₹1,380 Crores capital expenditure programme nearing commercialisation is targeted to expand (RFSS spooling) capacity to 4,000 MT by FY2026-27.

For FY2026-27, management expects strong growth across subsidiary operations and a firm rebound in standalone volumes, driving the Company towards peak utilisation targets as new manufacturing lines come online.

Ratnamani Finow Spooling Solutions (RFSS) is expanding spool manufacturing capacity from 1,500 MT to 4,000 MT annually via a new 52,000 sq. metre greenfield fabrication facility in Kutch, expected to materially strengthen execution capability and unlock larger project participation in H2 FY2026-27.

Ratnamani Middle East Company LLC obtained commercial registration and began setting up its cold-finished stainless steel manufacturing facility in Dammam from January 2026, with trial production targeted for Q1 FY2027-28 and commercial readiness to follow.

Greenfield joint venture project in Saudi Arabia (Ratnamani Middle East Company, LLC) is progressing rapidly, targeting trial production by Q1 FY2027-28, manufacturing cold-finished stainless steel seamless tubes and giving critical localised manufacturing status in the Saudi market.

₹820 Crores of the ₹1,380 Crores capex programme is earmarked for strategic international and group expansion, anchored by a new cold-finishing stainless steel seamless products plant via the Saudi Arabia joint venture (75% equity stake) in Dammam, to localise production and secure preferential bidding status in the Middle East.

Management flagged global commodity volatility, geopolitical uncertainties, and execution risks in large-scale projects as realities the Company must navigate, relying on a diversified portfolio, strong vendor approvals and disciplined capital allocation for resilience.
New greenfield coating plant in Odisha is progressing well: the internal coating line is already fully operational, and the external 3LPE coating plant is undergoing final trial runs.

Advanced construction of a new 1,00,000 MT Helical Submerged Arc Welded (HSAW) spiral pipe facility in Kutch, to produce pipes up to 120 inches in diameter in 18-metre lengths, built for the next generation of energy and infrastructure projects.

Management flagged continuing exposure to geopolitical volatility (Red Sea corridor disruptions, Middle East conflict), commodity price fluctuations, and execution challenges as risks it must navigate going into FY2026-27.

Strategic focus remains on product-mix optimisation and value enhancement, with a calibrated shift towards higher-margin, specialised product categories, alongside continued expansion of global market presence to capitalise on emerging energy and infrastructure capex cycles.

Ravi Technoforge is expanding via a greenfield high-speed hot forming facility in Rajkot targeting next-generation automotive products, drivetrain components and the large-volume rings segment for large OEM customers and the EV market.

Ratnamani Finow Spooling Solutions is scaling up via an 80,000 sq. metre fabrication facility with new equipment including Heavy Induction Bending Machines, expanding fabrication capacity from 1,500 MT to 4,000 MT for pipes up to 18 metres in length.

risks.note: Fluctuations in basic steel, stainless steel inputs and imported alloys directly impact margins; the Company relies on back-to-back procurement aligned with confirmed orders and ~200-day inventory buffers to absorb shocks.
Over 50% of stainless steel raw material requirements are currently imported, exposing the Company to global supply shocks, arbitrary export policies, and fluctuations in import duties.

Import of raw materials and export revenues expose the Company to currency fluctuations; managed via natural hedging from the import-export matrix and forward contracts per Forex Policy, with no speculative trading.

Global trade barriers, tariffs and supply-chain rerouting from regional conflicts are a persistent threat; the ongoing war in the Middle East has already raised freight, container and insurance costs and impacted exports, and a prolonged conflict would adversely affect revenues.
risks.risk: Geopolitical trade risk / ongoing Middle East war

risks.note: Increasing protectionism in the EU and US, including quota reductions, 50% tariffs and the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), could adversely impact exports and market access, given exports constitute a significant portion of the order book.
risks.risk: Trade protectionism and export market access

risks.note: The domestic carbon steel division is highly sensitive to infrastructure project execution velocity; administrative delays in state-level water distribution schemes or deferred environmental clearances for hydrocarbon pipelines cause unpredictable lumpiness in order booking and dispatches.

High dependence on electricity and CNG exposes operations to tariff revisions, demand penalties, supply constraints and volatile fuel costs, particularly for the energy-intensive seamless tube business.
Growing adoption of piercing-route manufacturing and increasing global overcapacity, especially from China and Asia, may intensify price competition and compress margins in commodity-grade segments.
risks.risk: Competition from alternative manufacturing technologies and overcapacity
